subject: Prod request shaping triggers client-visible 429s — urgent exec review
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <sre@acme.io>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production 429 spike — morning batch

Connor,

We started seeing a sharp rise in 429s and 2-3x tail latency for token-generation endpoints at ~08:50 PT. Our dashboards show an abrupt request shaping event paired with burst rejections — affecting our checkout flow. Sample trace ids attached and a CSV of recent requests is attached (acme-requests-20260719.csv).

Impact: ~8% failed checkouts, several merchant integrations failing. We suspect a change in how bursts are being allowed through the token bucket. Can you triage and escalate?

I can provide more logs and jump on a call.

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
SRE, Acme Commerce

Attachments: acme-requests-20260719.csv
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <sre@acme.io>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production 429 spike — morning batch

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the sample CSV.

Grace, looping you in to lead the technical triage. Initial plan: validate whether a config roll made last night altered burstwindow or safety valve thresholds, and if so, whether we can roll that change back or apply a temporary quota increase for Acme.

Alex, can you confirm whether the traffic shape is uniform across regions and if the traces include request headers x-client-id and x-request-id? That will speed the correlation. Also, please leave this thread open for exec-level updates — I've cc'd Marissa since this is impacting revenue.

I will coordinate a quick bridge if needed.

—Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Alex Mercer <sre@acme.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production 429 spike — morning batch

Investigated a few things and here's what I have so far.

Findings
- At 01:12 UTC (approx 00:12 PT last night) we rolled out a rate-limiter policy change to improve headroom for free-tier bursts; an unintended side-effect reduced the burst window multiplier for customers with custom quotas. The policy name is rate_shaper_v3.
- Acme's tenant-level quota was moved to the new policy path and now inherits a smaller burst allowance. On our side the token-bucket refill math is correct, but the policy parameter burst_multiplier was set from 3.0 to 0.8 during the rollout. That explains immediate 429s for short spikes.
- No underlying infra degradation; CPU and GPU utilization are normal. This is config/semantic regression.

Immediate mitigation options (recommended order)
1) Roll back rate_shaper_v3 to previous parameters (restore burst_multiplier=3.0) — this is a config-only rollback and should take effect within seconds after the config service syncs. Risk: none to infra, possible minor broader burst exposure for free-tier flows. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rate-limiter-rollback
2) If rollback is not acceptable, provision a temporary quota bump for Acme (tenant override) for 2 hours while we validate.
3) Apply a targeted policy override for the Acme client id (less desirable if there are many client ids).

I attached a diff of the policy change (ratepolicy-diff.txt) and a latency snapshot (latency-dashboard.png). I'm on standby to execute rollback — Connor, can you confirm executive approval to proceed with option 1 or 2?

Grace O'Connor
Director, Production Reliability
Redwood Inference
Attachments: ratepolicy-diff.txt, latency-dashboard.png
From: Alex Mercer <sre@acme.io>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production 429 spike — morning batch

Connor / Grace,

Thanks for the quick analysis — that aligns with what we see. We can accept a temporary tenant-level quota bump for the next 2 hours while you roll back. Please go ahead with the mitigation you prefer. We are on a call now and can validate traffic as soon as you flip the switch.

Trace samples and headers included in the earlier CSV; let me know if you need more. Appreciate the fast response.

Alex Mercer
SRE, Acme Commerce
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Exec: Approved temporary quota bump and post-incident actions

Team,

Thanks for triaging. Per Alex's confirmation, approve the following immediate actions:
- Grace: apply tenant-level quota override for Acme to restore pre-incident throughput for 2 hours, and proceed with a safe rollback of rate_shaper_v3 parameters to previous values within the same maintenance window. Coordinate with Connor for customer validation.
- Connor: notify Acme right after the override and request heap of traces for a post-mortem. If Acme requests credits for the impacted window, coordinate with Finance and Legal; I will approve credits up to $25k after the post-mortem if we determine this was our regression.
- Ops: capture a memory of the rollout (who pushed the change, PR id, runbook steps) and keep a live log for the incident timeline.

We will run a cross-functional post-mortem tomorrow. Grace, please include a suggested guardrail to prevent burst_multiplier regressions in future rollouts (validation tests / canary checks).

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Reliability and Escalations
Redwood Inference
